plan.title: Liver treated vs control: descriptive DE, no replicates
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is 1 treated vs 1 control liver sample from salmon-derived gene-level counts (12000 genes x 3 columns incl. gene symbol), with zero biological replication in either arm. The knowledge base flags this design explicitly (rule R-0003): with n=1 per group, no within-group variance/dispersion can be estimated, so no valid p-value exists. The plan therefore does QC on sample structure, filters low-count genes, computes DESeq2 median-of-ratios size factors for normalization, and reports DESCRIPTIVE log2 fold changes (treated vs control) with no inferential test and no FDR control — explicitly flagged as non-inferential throughout. A ranked (preranked) GSEA against MSigDB Hallmark (and Reactome as a secondary collection, both staged locally) is run on the descriptive log2FC ranking, itself descriptive/hypothesis-generating only, since no gene-level p-values exist to build a proper rank statistic. The final report states plainly that this design supports no significance calls and names what would be needed (biological replicates in each arm) to run a real inferential DESeq2/edgeR test.
